label: Blue Note
rationale: Sam Rivers' debut as a leader, recorded weeks after his brief tenure with the Miles Davis Quintet, is a consensus-cited landmark of inside-outside post-bop: Penguin Guide 4 stars, DownBeat 4 stars, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 4 stars, AllMusic 4.5 stars, and a permanent place in Blue Note's classic canon. The quartet — Jaki Byard, Ron Carter, and the 18-year-old Tony Williams — is pure session gravity, and the record fixed 'Beatrice' as a standard. Rivers' inside-outside language on this date is the bridge between the hard-bop mainstream and the avant-garde already represented in the canon (Out to Lunch!, Point of Departure, Dialogue — on all of which Rivers plays).

ballot.case_for: Rivers' debut as a leader carries overwhelming consensus — 4-to-4.5 stars across Penguin Guide, DownBeat, AllMusic, and Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide — and permanent standing in Blue Note's classic catalogue. Session gravity is exceptional: Ron Carter and the 18-year-old Tony Williams (two-thirds of the contemporaneous Miles Davis rhythm section, arriving weeks after Rivers' own Davis stint) plus Jaki Byard. The album fixed 'Beatrice' as an enduring standard, and Rivers' inside-outside language here is the audible bridge between the hard-bop mainstream and the already-canonical avant records he played on — Out to Lunch!, Point of Departure, Dialogue — making it exactly the record the rubric asks for: one that teaches the idiom and connects to what the canon already holds.
ballot.case_against: The honest against-case is thin but real. Rivers' inside-outside approach stretches tonal and harmonic boundaries enough that a listener oriented to the modal comfort of early-60s post-bop may find the angularity abrasive — relevant given John's standing calibration note on the avant-garde. One could also argue the elite rhythm section's gravity slightly overshadows Rivers' own conceptual authorship at moments. Sourcing is adequate but not deep (five sources, two of them bare identifiers), though the core facts — date, studio, personnel, ratings — are well corroborated.
ballot.disagreement: Reference 1 returned no judgment, so no substantive split exists; Reference 2 alone argued the case and landed on consensus_core/must_have. The ballot rests on a single reference voice plus the dossier evidence.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John treat this as a consensus-core must-have and admit it as the load-bearing Sam Rivers entry in the canon.
